result.process_description:
The MSPN sends a dismissal to the MSPO.
The MSPO reviews the dismissal.
The MSPO rejects the dismissal of the MSPN or The MSPO confirms the dismissal of the MSPN.

args.text: When a process description says that one participant sends information or a document to another participant, model the sending action as a message-flow send task in the sender's pool rather than as an ordinary task. An explicit alternative between outcomes should be represented by an exclusive gateway.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidelines already cover the send-task choice or the explicit alternative structure.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.

args.text: When the description presents mutually exclusive outcomes that converge, model their alternative paths with an exclusive gateway.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers the gateway needed for the described alternative outcomes.

result.rule: When the description presents mutually exclusive alternatives or says an activity may or may not occur, and the paths later continue in common: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway, and reconnect the alternative paths with an exclusive merge before their shared continuation.

When the description states that whether additional activities occur depends on the outcome of earlier work: Model the alternatives with an exclusive gateway, and label its outgoing sequence flows with the conditions that determine whether the additional activities occur.
When the description states that a condition determines whether an action or process path is needed: model the choice with an exclusive gateway and conditional branches for the possible outcomes.

When the description states that an action should be taken depending on the outcome of a condition: Model the condition with an exclusive gateway and represent each stated follow-up action as a task on its applicable branch.

args.text: When a description states mutually exclusive alternative outcomes that each follow separate activities and then lead to the same continuation, model the choice with an exclusive gateway and merge the alternative paths with an exclusive gateway.

trace.reason: Check the documented guidance for the alternative outcomes and missing exclusive merge before deciding how this relates to learned guidance.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use an exclusive merge for alternative paths; it does not wait for inactive alternatives.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use an exclusive split when exactly one data-based alternative runs. Add supported conditions and at most one default fallback.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Compare the model with the description; remove unsupported elements and retain every explicitly stated alternative, outcome and collaboration.
